# managed extension persistence and background actions

_status: experimental · owner: core · id: `extensions.persistence`_

## the one command

```
hosaka extensions trust my-extension --trusted-local --allow-storage --allow-managed-data
```

## why you care

Persistent applications own their databases and optional synchronization without embedding application code in core.

## what it does

Explicitly granted per-extension data directories, optional network checks, bounded authenticated binary files and supervised background actions. Database schemas, replication and secrets remain extension-owned. Existing v1 defaults and trusted-local non-sandbox semantics are unchanged.

## commands

- `/extensions trust <id> --trusted-local --allow-storage --allow-managed-data --allow-network --allow-background`

## entrypoints

- `POST /api/v1/extensions/{identifier}/files`
- `GET /api/v1/extensions/{identifier}/files/{name}`

## what success looks like / what failure looks like

if it works, it's quiet. if it doesn't, expect one of:

- missing managed grant, stale approval, root/public or safe mode refuses access
- uploads exceeding size/time bounds fail explicitly
- background failures are logged; revoked jobs are cancelled

dig deeper:
- `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8421/api/v1/events?feature_id=extensions.persistence&limit=20 | jq`
